---
title: "Configuration"
---

You configure `jupyter-positron-server` through environment variables, and the
JupyterHub side through `jupyterhub_config.py`. This page covers both, and the
settings that matter most when you run Positron Server for a group of users, such
as a class. Treat the suggested values as starting points, then measure your own
hardware and number of users and adjust.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE` | Path to a license file that `jupyter-positron-server` passes to `positron-server` as `--license-key-file`. On Positron Server 2026.09.0 and newer, this file can be a raw `license.lic`. Leave it unset when the license file sits in the activation directory at `<positron-server-path>/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license.lic`, which is where `positron-server` looks by default. |
| `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` | URL of the JupyterHub minting endpoint that issues short-lived signed license tokens. Applies to Positron Server 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2 only. Takes precedence over `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE`. See [Verifier setup](verifier_get_started.qmd). |
| `POSITRON_CONNECTION_TOKEN` | Sets the connection token that Positron Server validates on every request. Defaults to a random token for each session. Set it per session from a `pre_spawn_hook` to land students in Positron Server through `Spawner.default_url`. Do not set one fixed value for all sessions. See [Start students in Positron Server](#start-students-in-positron-server). |
| `POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS` | JSON object of Positron settings that students cannot change. See [Admin-enforced settings](#admin-enforced-settings). |
| `POSITRON_HOST` | Host address for Positron Server to bind to. Defaults to `127.0.0.1`. |
| `JSP_DEFAULT_FOLDER` | Directory that Positron Server opens. Defaults to `JUPYTERHUB_ROOT_DIR`, then `HOME`. |
| `JSP_POSITRON_LAUNCHER_DISABLED` | Set to any value to hide the Positron tile in the JupyterLab launcher. |

On Positron Server 2026.09.0 and newer, a license needs no environment variable
at all. `positron-server` finds `license.lic` in its own activation directory.
Both license variables are for deployments that keep the file somewhere else, or
that still run on 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2.

::: callout-important
Each assignment to `c.Spawner.environment` replaces the whole dictionary, so use
`.update()` to add a variable. On TLJH, the install script sets `PATH` in
`c.SystemdSpawner.environment`. A setting on the spawner class takes precedence
over `c.Spawner`, so on TLJH, JupyterHub ignores `c.Spawner.environment`. Use
`c.SystemdSpawner.environment.update()` instead, in a file in
`jupyterhub_config.d/` whose name sorts after `positron.py`.
:::

## Start students in Positron Server

A single-user server opens JupyterLab by default, and students reach Positron Server
from the launcher tile. `Spawner.default_url` changes where a session lands.

Positron Server validates a connection token on every HTTP and WebSocket request.
The launcher tile works because it carries that token as a `tkn` query parameter.
A bare `/positron` URL carries no token, so Positron Server answers `403 Forbidden`.

The token protects the port that Positron Server listens on, so only the student who owns the session can connect to it.
To land students in Positron Server, make a new token when each session starts.
Put it in the session environment and in the landing URL:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
import secrets

def positron_token_hook(spawner):
    token = secrets.token_hex(16)
    # Copy the dictionary. The configured value can be shared by every spawner.
    spawner.environment = {**spawner.environment, "POSITRON_CONNECTION_TOKEN": token}
    spawner.default_url = f"/positron/?tkn={token}"

c.Spawner.pre_spawn_hook = positron_token_hook
```

On TLJH, put this code in a file in `/opt/tljh/config/jupyterhub_config.d/`, then run `sudo tljh-config reload`.
Do not set one fixed token for all sessions.
Every student sees the token in their own URL.
On TLJH, all sessions share one host, so a student with the token can open the Positron Server of another student.
Students can still reach JupyterLab at `/user/<username>/lab` when they need the notebook interface.

## Admin-enforced settings

`POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS` lets administrators lock Positron settings so
students cannot override them through the Settings UI, or by editing
`settings.json` directly. Locked settings appear grayed out with a policy
indicator. Enforced settings survive profile changes, workspace switches, and
direct edits to `~/.positron-server/data/User/settings.json`.

**Requirements**: `jupyter-positron-server` 0.0.4 or newer, and Positron Server
2026.07.1-5 or newer.

Two settings come up often for coursework:

- **`ai.enabled`**: set to `false` to turn off every Positron AI feature at once. To
  turn features off one at a time, see the
  [Positron AI configuration reference](https://positron.posit.co/ai-configuration.html).
- **`extensions.autoUpdate`**: set to `false` to hold extension versions steady across
  a class for the length of a term.

On TLJH, create a config file that locks both:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
cat > /opt/tljh/config/jupyterhub_config.d/positron_enforced.py << 'EOF'
c.SystemdSpawner.environment.update({
    'POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS': '{"ai.enabled":false,"extensions.autoUpdate":false}'
})
EOF
```

The file name `positron_enforced.py` sorts after `positron.py`, so the update runs
after the install script sets `PATH`. On other spawners, use
`c.Spawner.environment.update(...)` in `jupyterhub_config.py`.

Sessions that are already running keep their settings until a student starts a
new session.

## Memory requirements

Allocate at least 2.5 GB of RAM per Positron Server session. A Positron Server
session uses more memory than an RStudio session or a plain Jupyter kernel, and the
right amount depends on the size of the workload:

- **Light**: single console, few extensions, simple scripts, basic app development
- **Standard**: runtime switching, multiple consoles, multiple extensions, app development
- **Heavy**: memory-intensive extensions such as file watchers or language servers, multiple concurrent apps, large datasets

Use the table below to match each workload level to its minimum and recommended
memory allocation.

| Workload | Minimum | Recommended |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| Light | 2 GB | 2.5 GB |
| Standard | 2.5 GB | 4 GB |
| Heavy | 4 GB | 6 GB or more |

Signs of insufficient memory include slow runtime switching, extensions that fail
to install, degraded app performance, and crashes during memory-intensive
operations.

::: callout-note
For the full guidance this section summarizes, see the Positron Pro
[memory allocation FAQ](https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/user/positron/reference/faq.html#allocate-sufficient-memory-for-your-positron-pro-session).
:::

### Cap memory and CPU per session

To enforce the recommended allocation for a standard workload, set limits in
`jupyterhub_config.py`:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
c.Spawner.mem_limit = '4G'
c.Spawner.cpu_limit = 1
```

`mem_limit` is a hard cap, not a share.
The spawner stops a session that reaches the cap, so a value below the recommended allocation produces crashes during memory-intensive work.
The 2 GB floor suits a light workload only.

On TLJH, set the same limits through `tljh-config`:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
sudo tljh-config set limits.memory 4G
sudo tljh-config set limits.cpu 1
sudo tljh-config reload
```

## Hub license minting (deprecated)

Hub license minting is a former way of working, scoped to Positron Server
2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2, and not recommended for a new deployment. Positron
Server 2026.09.0 and newer validate `license.lic` directly and need no minting
service. See [Verifier setup](verifier_get_started.qmd) only if you are
deploying that exact version range.
